subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally preserve session-level `/exec` defaults, but the reported behavior is security-sensitive because operator config changes can be shadowed by older session state.

options.title: Make config an upper bound
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with focused migration/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep persistent session overrides
options.body: Document that authorized `/exec` session defaults are sticky and require an explicit reset or repair flow when operators change policy.

options.title: Add reset or doctor first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing reset or doctor repair path before changing resolver precedence for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config an upper bound
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with focused migration/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and focused precedence tests points to this owner path.
